Markus —

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form. Our legal team flagged the indemnity section (Section 12) and sent a redline (attached). Two specific items they want clarity on:

1) The proposed customer indemnity for third-party IP claims appears broad — it doesn’t limit to direct use of the Service (it refers to any use of Customer Data) and doesn’t exclude claims that arise from Customer’s modification of the Service. Can Redwood confirm scope?

2) We’d like Redwood to accept an indemnity for third-party infringement claims where the claim arises from the Service (not Customer models or Customer-provided data). If Redwood can’t accept full IP indemnity, ByteArc is open to a narrow mutual patent carveout plus a defined mitigation/defense process.

Can you share Redwood’s preferred language or a compromise proposal? We’re trying to keep the deal moving; target signature week of 5/21.

Thanks for the context. I drafted three options below (attached detailed markup): Redwood_Proposed_Indemnity_4.3.docx.

Option A (Legal-favored — full indemnity for Service infringement):
- Redwood indemnifies Customer for third-party claims alleging the Service, as delivered by Redwood, directly infringes a third party’s patent/copyright/trademark.
- Exclusions: (i) claims arising from Customer’s modifications or combination with third-party products; (ii) claims based on Customer Data or prompts that include third-party proprietary content; (iii) open-source license claims unless caused by Redwood-modified OSS.
- Remedy: Redwood controls defense, with Customer able to participate at its expense; Redwood’s indemnity capped at the fees paid under the Order Form in prior 12 months (negotiable).

Option B (Commercial compromise):
- Same as A, but cap equals 2x fees in prior 12 months and Redwood requires Customer to demonstrate that the alleged infringing use is within the documented scope of Service usage.

Option C (Carveout + process):
- No broad indemnity. Instead: (i) mutual promise to avoid enforcement of asserted patents for model outputs (mutual patent peace) and (ii) formal cooperation/triage process where Redwood pursues mitigation steps but does not accept open-ended tort liability.

Questions for Sales:
- Risk appetite on cap (1x fees vs 2x vs unlimited for covered claims).
- Is ByteArc using Service to host their own trained models or only as an API consumer? (this affects exclusion scope).

I can circulate the marked MSA with Option B language if you want to offer a near-term compromise.

—Lauren

Agree with Lauren — Option B is the right commercial path. A few practical notes:

- ByteArc is trialing a retrieval-augmented search use case (they’re sending customer data into prompts, not training new models). That means we should be able to hold that claims related to Customer models are out of scope.
- Recommend cap = 2x ARR (for the first year, that’s ~$350k) but limit to direct damages only (defense costs separate, Redwood controls defense).
- If we make this concession, ask for reciprocal commitments: customer must keep detailed prompt logs for triage and must not modify the Service. Also request a hold-harmless for downstream customer-facing apps integrating outputs if those apps publish third-party content — i.e., ByteArc remains responsible for their productization of outputs.

I can lead the commercial call with Olivia next week.

Olivia —

Thanks for the redline and the quick turnaround. We reviewed internally and have a compromise we think is fair and should keep your counsel comfortable: attached is a proposed indemnity clause (Redwood_Proposed_Indemnity_4.3.docx). High level:

- Redwood will indemnify ByteArc for third-party claims alleging the Service, as provided by Redwood under the Order Form, directly infringes a third party’s patent, copyright, or trademark.
- Exclusions: claims arising from (i) Customer modifications to the Service, (ii) Customer-provided models or code, or (iii) Customer Data that includes third-party proprietary content introduced by Customer.
- Cap: Redwood’s liability for covered IP indemnity is limited to 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months (direct damages only). Redwood will control the defense and will advance reasonable defense costs.
- Process: we propose a 3-step triage: immediate notice, Redwood-led investigation & mitigation, and (if the claim cannot be resolved) defense led by Redwood with cooperation from ByteArc.

We think this balances risk and keeps the deal moving. Attached is the marked clause. If that looks okay, Marissa will set up a short call to finalize and we can push to signature.

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_Indemnity_4.3.docx

Best,
